newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NOL to decide on alliance in 6 mos - paper.
newsitem.headline: NOL to decide on alliance in 6 mos - paper.

text.p: Neptune Orient Lines (NOL) will decide within six months which vessel-sharing alliance to join, the daily Straits Times newspaper said on Friday.
It quoted NOL deputy chief executive officer Lim How Teck as saying: "We have yet to decide which alliance to join, or what decision to take. We have to study the pros and cons."
"I think it should probably be decided within six months."

NOL this week announced a proposed US$825 million takeover of American carrier APL Ltd. APL belongs to the Global Alliance with Japan's Mitsui O.S.K., Hong Kong's OOCL, and Nedlloyd of the Netherlands.
NOL is a member of the rival Grand Alliance, with Britain's P&O, Germany's Hapag-Lloyd and Japan's NYK, the Straits Times said.

The alliances are a mainstay of the global shipping industry and emerged about two years ago when carriers decided to coordinate sailing schedules and share vessel space to reduce costs, the Straits Times said.
